purpose: One scenario model for manually approved project totals, candidate impact reviews, and the website; unknowns and all project indicators are retained.

assumptions.unknown_mw: Unspecified datacenter MW preserves the source value or source range without PUE conversion. Reclassify from source wording where possible. PUE conversion is applied only when the source explicitly identifies the MW as IT power. The same rule is used in reviews, approved results and the website.
assumptions.grid_mw: Connection envelope only. Scenario equivalent assumes the allocated share is deployed as facility capacity; not measured demand.
assumptions.unknown_baseline: Gross site envelope is retained; additional capacity range is 0 to gross unless comparable installed baseline is known.
assumptions.overlap: Use one physical envelope; possible containment is assumed containment for aggregation, with the tenant retained in the project indicator.
assumptions.interpretation: Cumulative commissioned capacity since the fixed baseline; energy is a steady annual equivalent at that capacity. Annual additions, additional deployment after the assessment year, and capacity still to deliver are separate exports. No second utilization ramp.
assumptions.electrical_output: Facility-side nameplate capacity proxy, including cooling and auxiliary loads. Explicit peak claims use the declared inverse empirical peak/nameplate sensitivity; source MW and basis are retained. Phased MW is deployed capacity, not actual peak. Energy uses the original peak denominator when supplied.
assumptions.unknown_timing: Undated scopes use stage lead times to shape High, compressed to full by 2035. Stated also selects undated campus envelopes containing an executing, source-dated phase in the same project, independently of that phase MW. Model dates remain distinct from source dates.
assumptions.grid_timing: An explicitly linked grid date floors first operation for the same scope in Low/Stated, except already observed deliveries. Requested/unknown allocation has a zero lower case only there. Grid MW never caps load MW. High ignores grid constraints; retain source grid fields and overlap links.
assumptions.full_capacity_timing: A usable scoped full-build target is honored over generic stage and buildout durations. Infer first operation within the remaining window and shorten the proxy ramp when needed; never create unobserved historical commissioning. Only contradictory scoped evidence (later construction/first operation/grid availability) or an already elapsed target can move modelled completion. Preserve source values and expose evidence conflicts. An actual full-delivery event is a step, never a fabricated historical ramp. High separately compresses any later completion to 2035. Superseded targets are not current anchors.
assumptions.scenario_selection: Scenario IDs remain unchanged. Low requires the scope own current source date and decision=yes. Stated selects current source dates and the explicit executing_campus_full_by_horizon rule. High selects all active announced MW and reaches full build-out by 2035.

phasing.locator: Annual and Peak Electricity Use; updated 2026-02-24; operational-capacity ramp paragraph
phasing.use: Retain five years as a provisional physical-buildout proxy for staged/unknown scopes only. Known single-phase deliveries and scoped first/full schedules replace it. Do not interpret it as both construction and electricity-use ramp.
phasing.limitation: EPRI operational ramp is not direct evidence for physical commissioning. National Grid/Regen phase examples support a multi-year buildout, but five years is an uncalibrated adaptation; explicit phase schedules take precedence.

phasing_crosscheck.locator: November 2025, pp. 27–30, delivery timeframes and DFES modelling methodology
phasing_crosscheck.use: Supports phased project-pipeline modelling and source-specific schedules where available.
phasing_crosscheck.limitation: UK interviews show variation, including shorter ramps. They do not establish a universal 100 MW breakpoint.

construction.locator: Energy and AI (2025), The outlook for energy demand from data centres
construction.use: Use 2–3 years from stated construction start to first operation when no operation date is supplied.
construction.limitation: Adaptation of IEA typical 2–3-year development time to an annual construction-start anchor. Excludes prior permitting/grid lead time; not a deadline or guarantee.

pue.use: 1.1 and 1.5 are technology sensitivity cases; a documented local design PUE replaces the upper case.
pue.limitation: The source discusses hyperscale around 1.1 and older enterprise 1.5 or higher. This is not an exhaustive range or Nordic confidence interval; design PUE is not measured annual PUE.

annual_use.locator: Facility load-shape analysis and Figure 3; updated 2026-02-24
annual_use.use: Annual/nameplate 0.57–0.75; annual/realized-peak 0.88–0.94; peak/nameplate 0.62–0.80. Multiply deployment only once.
annual_use.limitation: Small anonymous US sample, not a universal AI utilization factor. Inverting peak/nameplate to infer capacity is our explicit sensitivity application, not an observed project nameplate.

metrics.use: Separate nominal IT, facility nameplate/service capacity, active capacity and realized peak.
metrics.limitation: Preserve uncertain source definitions. The facility-to-IT interval is a sensitivity, not proof of the actual electrical denominator.

pipeline_selection.locator: November 2025, pp. 28–30, baseline/pipeline research and scenario treatment
pipeline_selection.use: Use a project inventory, planning/connection evidence and explicit scenario selection. Reconcile overlapping project and connection records.
pipeline_selection.limitation: Supports the approach, not our exact Low/Stated/High definitions or the 2035 horizon. These are conditional policy selections, not externally estimated probabilities.

stage_lead_times.locator: IEA outlook paragraph; National Grid/Regen pp. 26–28
stage_lead_times.use: Own provisional sensitivity assumptions: concept/unclear 2–5 years to construction, planned 1–3, permitted 0–1; then 2–3 construction years. Under construction without a usable start: 0–2 remaining years (zero means possible later in the assessment calendar year).
stage_lead_times.limitation: Sources support separating delivery, phases and grid constraints, not these exact stage intervals. They are not observed Nordic durations or confidence intervals; calibrate against documented milestones of completed, comparable phases.

method_4_1.use: Defines horizon completion, executing-campus selection, removal of grid MW caps, open lower-bound claims and superseded-target treatment.
method_4_1.limitation: Explicit scenario policy, not empirical delivery probabilities or confirmation that announced capacity will be built. Grid-date evidence can still constrain Low/Stated.

assumptions.annual_use_by_type: Load factor relative to nameplate depends on facility type (EPRI 2026 p.15: 75% hyperscale facility, 57% co-location average). type_assumptions gives one value per type category; nameplate_annual_fraction is only used when type is unknown.
assumptions.phase_timing: Known single-phase delivery is a step at its own commissioning date. Undated campus with an included same-project executing phase (observed construction or decision=yes, own operation/construction/full date) starts at the phase first operation; construction-only uses 2–3 years. Early campus path uses five years capped at 2035; late path is linear through 2035. The phase need not have MW. Planned phases without FID, grid dates alone, other projects and old operating baselines do not qualify. Low never inherits this campus selection. Quantified phases provide early floors using max-envelope overlap accounting.
assumptions.investment_decision: decision=yes means an evidenced investment decision for that scope: an explicit final investment decision or observed construction start of that phase. Low 2030 counts only such figures.
assumptions.buildout_energy: Electricity at full build-out is the net capacity envelope times the type load factor and 8760 h, without a second ramp. High 2035 equals this full build-out equivalent.
assumptions.capacity_without_upper_limit: at_least without mw_max supplies a known lower bound and an open upper bound. Convert and subtract comparable baselines normally; display ≥ X for projects and sums containing open bounds. Never classify the known minimum as missing MW.
assumptions.horizon: High includes all active announced MW fully by timeline.end_year (2035), after existing-capacity and overlap accounting. Its endpoint equals full build-out; shorten later schedules to this horizon. This is an upper envelope, not a forecast.
assumptions.superseded_targets: A later source for the same/comparable scope that omits or replaces an earlier target makes that target undated (timing_status=superseded). Preserve the historical date and MW, cite both sources and their temporal ordering in notes. Access date alone does not establish a newer statement. Actual events are not superseded targets; separate mixed scopes.

type_assumptions.purpose: Type-specific annual use factors for the single scenario model. The website displays the computed result without a separate PUE, timing or scenario calculation.
type_assumptions.origin: Annual load factors from the previous method table, with peak-relative factors from EPRI 2026 p.15. PUE sensitivity is defined once in assumptions.pue and sourced claim-level pue.
type_assumptions.model_use: Annual energy uses phased capacity x type load factor x 8760, or the peak-relative factor for explicit peak claims. Unknown types retain the generic sensitivity. PUE uses assumptions.pue and any sourced claim-level design PUE for all outputs.

Hyperscale.load_factor_source: EPRI 2026; observed large hyperscale facility annual load factor of 75% relative to nameplate capacity. Shehabi et al. 2024 used only as supporting evidence on high relative hyperscale server operational time.
Hyperscale.peak_load_factor_source: EPRI 2026 p.15: annual load factor relative to realized peak 94% for the hyperscale facility.

Hyperscale_AI.load_factor_source: EPRI 2026; hyperscale observed annual load factor of 75% relative to nameplate capacity. Shehabi et al. 2024 distinguishes AI training and inference operational time. Regen/National Grid DSO 2025 notes AI training is relatively flat while inference is peakier.
Hyperscale_AI.peak_load_factor_source: EPRI 2026 p.15: annual load factor relative to realized peak 94% for the hyperscale facility.

AI_HPC.load_factor_source: Shehabi et al. 2024; AI training server operational time assumed at 80%, varied between 75-85%. EPRI 2026 provides facility-level support that hyperscale load factors can be high but below nameplate.
AI_HPC.peak_load_factor_source: No type-specific observation; EPRI 2026 p.15 range across hyperscale (94%) and co-location (88%).

Colocation_AI.load_factor_source: EPRI 2026; smaller multi-tenant co-location facilities averaged 57% annual load factor relative to nameplate. Regen/National Grid DSO 2025 notes colocation load is relatively consistent due to tenant diversity, while AI workloads may increase variability.
Colocation_AI.peak_load_factor_source: EPRI 2026 p.15: annual load factor relative to realized peak 88% on average for co-location facilities.

Colocation.load_factor_source: EPRI 2026; smaller multi-tenant co-location facilities averaged 57% annual load factor relative to nameplate capacity. Regen/National Grid DSO 2025 supports relatively consistent colocation load due to flat storage/cloud use cases and tenant diversity.
Colocation.peak_load_factor_source: EPRI 2026 p.15: annual load factor relative to realized peak 88% on average for co-location facilities.

Research_SMR.load_factor_source: Placeholder aligned with AI/HPC-oriented facilities. Concept entries are not translated into annual electricity use unless IT/grid-side load is specified.
Research_SMR.peak_load_factor_source: No type-specific observation; EPRI 2026 p.15 range across hyperscale (94%) and co-location (88%).

migration.duplicate_candidate_merged: Nebius Lappeenranta -> P035; C040 is Nebius, not XTX
migration.related_candidate: SVG-Undheim linked to P023; no separate quantified addition until identity is resolved
migration.historical_ids: Retired IDs and full field-review history remain in source_commit; do not recycle IDs.

geography_note: Inherited WGS84 display polygons; origin/redistribution rights unresolved. Municipal coordinates are approximate. Unknown bidding zone stays unassigned; never infer it from a project name.

basis.grid: Grid connection or available supply envelope
basis.unspecified: Data-centre MW without stated IT/facility/grid basis
basis.density: Rack density; not a site MW total

field_notes.first_year / last_year: Earliest/latest year of the event specified by timing; never insert an assumed model date. Both endpoints enter timing sensitivity.
field_notes.mw / mw_max: Reported MW; mw_max only for an explicit range. Unit is electrical MW except backup/generation/density, which are not load inputs.
field_notes.pue: Optional local design upper PUE used as a model assumption, not claimed measured annual performance.
field_notes.source_ids: Semicolon-separated IDs from sources.csv; the same source can support several rows.
field_notes.baseline_id: Same-measure installed capacity claim, only subtracted if baseline_scope=existing_known.
field_notes.parent_id: An enveloping capacity claim; included_in/possibly_included_in prevent double counting.
field_notes.timing_status: superseded retains an old target in source fields but excludes its dates from all current timing anchors. Requires a later source for the same or comparable scope which omits or replaces the date, documented in notes. Never set on actual events; separate mixed scopes.

workflow.origin: Template plus country overlays and audit/discover/review/promote/build from e3b85cc; discovery routes and frozen inputs from 9779acc. Integrated into one prompt and the existing CLI; historical manual queues are not restored.
workflow.scope: New datacenter load: greenfield datacenters and evidenced new phases or expansions at existing sites. Exclude ordinary server rooms, unlocated GPU purchases and multi-site national investment totals as separate facilities.

evidence_priority.capacity: Exact scoped technical or operator statement; retain ambiguity when the measure is unspecified.
evidence_priority.grid: Grid operator or regulatory document; distinguish requested, reserved and contracted connection.
evidence_priority.permission: Authority decision or registry; an application is not a permit.
evidence_priority.execution: Observed operator/contractor execution or municipal inspection; commitment applies to the evidenced phase.
evidence_priority.secondary: Trade and local reporting may establish candidates or cited estimates; newer weak evidence does not automatically replace a stronger source.

workflow.id_floor_origin: Highest P/C/S IDs across all CSV history through 9a08c22; later records are retained and new IDs advance above the live maximum.

manual_candidate_approval.authority: Explicit human approval of named project IDs in the current chat. An inventory or workflow-change request does not approve candidates.
manual_candidate_approval.review: Present sources, source MW, additional capacity envelope and per-scenario MW/TWh impact, unknowns and overlap. Individual conditional impacts are not automatically additive.
manual_candidate_approval.apply: review creates a temporary snapshot; approve requires that unchanged snapshot and explicitly approved IDs. Inventory apply cannot promote candidates. Rebuild all approved outputs together after approval.

register_if_all: identified physical site (municipality and locality or plot)
named datacenter actor that will build or operate the facility, or a named end user (not only a landowner, energy, wind or real-estate company offering a site)
new capacity: greenfield or an evidenced new phase/expansion
site-specific evidence beyond marketing: land agreement, zoning/asemakaava/reguleringsplan for this datacenter, EIA/YVA, building or environmental permit, grid agreement, or observed construction
keep_out: operating facilities without an evidenced expansion (register only as baseline when an expansion is registered)
datacenter-ready land or grid-ready sites marketed by energy, wind, real-estate or site developers without a named datacenter actor
concept studies and municipal zoning initiatives without a named datacenter operator or end user
inclusion_rule.leads: Out-of-scope leads found during a run go to the run log (runs/), not the register. Existing register rows that fail the rule are set to record_type=out_of_scope with a reason in notes; they keep their ID for identity matching and can return to candidate with new evidence.
inclusion_rule.out_of_scope: Kept for identity only: never in approved totals, candidate reviews, worklists or the website.

workflow.timing_followup: prepare and check expose per-claim timing gaps, scoped existing excerpts, search questions and review keys. Resolve with source data or record a dated Timing review in capacity.notes using the current key and a substantive remaining-uncertainty explanation. No parallel review register.

tracker.purpose: Presentation of the same manually approved model result used in chat. No independent site calculation. Local site installation is separate from external publishing.
tracker.scope: All approved project indicators, including unknown MW, missing geography and inactive/operating history. The capacity model determines additional MW; display status never invents capacity.

actor_classification.purpose: Project-level actor identity and global headquarters; separate from ultimate control, fund domicile, investor capital and capacity assumptions.

hq_groups.mixed: HQ in and outside project country

actor_classification.region_note: Europe is the explicit broader list here, including Cyprus and transcontinental Russia and Türkiye. On the map, Domestic means HQ in the project country, Other Europe means HQ in another country on this list, and Outside Europe means a known HQ outside it. Unknown HQ countries match none of these. EU and EU/EEA remain separate data facets. HQ highlights match at least one evidenced actor HQ and do not imply ownership or legal sovereignty.
actor_classification.coverage_rule: Survey every non-out_of_scope project in the chosen country. Missing rows remain unknown. A project has unknown overall HQ origin if any relevant actor is unresolved or lacks a country.
actor_classification.counting_rule: Actors join by project_id, never claim_id. Multiple matching actors select a project once. Existing campus/customer capacity allocations are not reassigned by actor filters.

timeline.meaning: End-of-year additions after the fixed 2025 year-end baseline. Assessment date is the latest of this configured floor, capacity status dates and accessed dates of sources directly linked to capacity; never the system clock or an actor-only review. Actual scoped events preserve historical additions.
